evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.35: quōs adhūc mihi magistrātūs populus Rōmānus mandāvit
terms.comment: magistrātum gerere, to hold office (Traupman 179); petere, to stand for it (Traupman 180); magistrātū abīre, to leave it. Also the official himself (see government).

terms.gloss: an office, a post of honour
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.35: ut mihi illum honōrem tum nōn sōlum datum, sed etiam crēditum et commissum putārem
terms.comment: The office as an honour the people confers; in the plural the offices of a public career. Cicero writes honōs, later authors honor (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ita quaestor sum factus ut mihi illum honōrem tum nōn sōlum datum, sed etiam crēditum et commissum putārem
phrases.english: when I was made quaestor, I felt that the office had not only been given to me but entrusted and committed to my care

phrases.latin: populō, quī stultus honōrēs saepe dat indignīs
phrases.english: the people, which is foolish enough often to give office to the unworthy
